summary.title: Sprint 5 — Frontend React Phase 1
summary.one_liner: Bootstrap React app with GameStateProvider and fully interactive Equinox HUD over live backend API
summary.problem_statement: The backend is complete through Sprint 4 with a full REST API surface, but there is no frontend. Sprint 5 bootstraps the React application and delivers the first player-facing component — the Equinox HUD — fully functional over live backend data.
summary.success_criteria: React app connects to Fastify backend, GameStateProvider manages all API state, Equinox HUD renders all elements (stamina, energy, stance, personality, path) with full interactivity and armor-themed aesthetic

commander_intent.desired_end_state: A player sees a polished, armor-themed HUD displaying their real game state with all interactive elements working — feels like part of the game world, not a developer prototype
non_negotiables: HUD connects to real backend API, not mock data
All HUD elements from spec implemented and interactive
Visual aesthetic matches armor/leather design language
boundaries: Phase 1 frontend only — no town scene, dialogue UI, or combat UI
Toolchain choice deferred to outline phase

in: React project initialization and build toolchain setup
GameStateProvider context wrapping API state synchronization
Complete Equinox HUD component with all interactive elements
Development proxy or CORS setup for backend communication

constraints: Must consume existing REST API without backend modifications
Existing backend runs on Fastify, port 3000

assumptions.assumption: Existing API endpoints provide all data the HUD needs
assumptions.basis: Sprint 4 completed full API surface with game state, player, personality, and narrative endpoints
Single-player local dev environment; no multi-user scenario yet

assumptions.assumption: HUD design spec in handoff doc is complete enough to implement from
assumptions.basis: Spec lists all elements but may need creative decisions on exact interaction behavior
Standard dev setup for React + API server

decision_posture.notes: Outline recommends, user approves build tool, styling, and folder layout
Outline recommends, user approves color palette, component styling, layout
Outline recommends, user approves state management patterns and API integration

open_questions: React toolchain choice (Vite vs Next.js, styling approach)
Frontend project structure (monorepo subfolder vs separate project)
How GameStateProvider handles state refresh (polling, event-driven, or on-demand)
Exact interaction behavior for path selector
